title: Closing a project: activities, inputs, outputs and RACI
blurb: Place a closure action in the right closing a project activity, for planned or premature closure, and answer RACI questions on evaluating the project.
question: At the end of the final stage, the project manager reviews the issue register, spots a lesson about late user involvement and puts it in a report prepared with the team. Which closing activity is this, and who is accountable for it?

teach.body: Closing a project gives a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed and the project's objectives, or approved changes to them, are recognized as achieved. If the board ends the project early, it makes sure the project still closes in an orderly way. It is the last part of the final stage, not a stage of its own. The project manager prepares closure; the board authorizes it in directing a project.

teach.caption: Fig 19.1: one of the two 'prepare' activities is used, then the same three activities follow.

head: Activity
Key actions
Output
rows: Confirm the project can close; update the project plan with actuals; close the project log; secure and archive records; prepare closure communications
Record the premature close request; salvage useful work; make products safe; agree what is complete or abandoned
Pass products to the operational and maintenance environment; confirm acceptance; check post-project benefits reviews are planned
Compare with the baselined PID and current version; compare estimates with actuals; review the project log for lessons with the PMT
Brief the board on performance; confirm readiness; highlight concessions; recommend recognition
teach.caption: Post-project benefits reviews are planned in the project, not carried out by it.
Either way the project still confirms acceptance, evaluates itself and requests closure. Only the board can trigger a premature close.

head: Activity
Role

teach.caption: From the official RACI extracts for table 19.2 (19.6). The executive is accountable for an activity the PM carries out.

teach.body: The project manager is responsible for creating all the new management products in closing a project, such as the end project report and lessons report, but may delegate the work. The board decides: it may trigger a premature close, and it authorizes closure in directing a project. Checking that post-project benefits reviews are planned may be done by the senior user, whose commitment to benefits continues after the project ends.

teach.body: In the final stage of the Engineering Skills Centre, project manager Leah Whitfield hands the building and its manuals to Craig Dunmore's estates team, and the senior user checks that reviews of apprentice numbers after opening are planned. She compares the asbestos and structural estimates with actuals, reviews the project log for lessons with the team, and writes the end project report. Executive Elaine Fairbairn is accountable; the senior supplier and project assurance are consulted. Leah closes the log, archives the records and asks the board to close the project.

teach.text: Traps: (1) Closing a project is part of the final stage, not a separate stage. (2) Only the project board triggers a premature close; the PM prepares it. (3) Reviewing the project log for lessons is evaluate the project; CLOSING the project log is prepare planned closure. (4) Recommending a supplier or team for future work, and suggesting recognition, belongs to request project closure.

items: Five activities: prepare planned closure, prepare premature closure, confirm project acceptance, evaluate the project, request project closure.
Premature closure: record the request, salvage useful work, make products safe, agree what is complete or abandoned.
Confirm acceptance: products pass to operations and maintenance; benefits reviews planned.
Evaluate the project: executive accountable, PM responsible, senior supplier and assurance consulted; business layer not involved.

summary: You can now place any closure action in the right closing a project activity, for planned and premature closure alike. You can also answer RACI questions on evaluating the project from the official rows.

A.q: Tarnside College is opening its Engineering Skills Centre. In the final stage, project manager Leah Whitfield compares the original estimates for asbestos removal and structural works with the actual figures, so that future college projects can be estimated more accurately. Which 'closing a project' activity is she carrying out?
A.why: In evaluate the project, the PM can improve estimating for future projects by analysing this project's estimates against its actual progress (19.4.4).

whyNot.0: Prepare planned closure confirms the project can close, updates the plan with actuals and archives records; analysing estimates for future use is evaluation.
whyNot.2: Confirm project acceptance hands products to operations and confirms acceptance.
whyNot.3: Request project closure briefs the board and asks for closure; the analysis comes before it.

A.q: Owen Pryce, Greystack Build's contracts director, is the senior supplier on the Tarnside project. Leah Whitfield asks for his view on how the building contract performed while she evaluates the project. Under the RACI for 'evaluate the project', what is the senior supplier's part?
A.why: In evaluate the project the senior supplier is consulted, as is project assurance; the executive is accountable and the PM responsible (19.6, table 19.2).

whyNot.0: The executive is accountable for evaluate the project.
whyNot.1: The project manager is responsible for evaluate the project.
whyNot.2: The senior supplier gives input before the evaluation is finished, so it is consulted, not merely informed.

A.q: At the end of the Tarnside project, the finished centre, its operating manuals and its maintenance contracts are handed over to Craig Dunmore's estates team, who will look after the building. Sunita Rao, the senior user, checks that reviews of apprentice numbers after opening are planned. Which 'closing a project' activity is this?
A.why: In confirm project acceptance, products pass to the operational and maintenance environment and acceptance is confirmed; checking post-project benefits reviews are planned may be done by the senior user (19.4.3).

whyNot.1: Prepare planned closure confirms the project can close and archives records; the handover itself is acceptance.
whyNot.2: Evaluate the project reviews performance against the PID and produces the end project report.
whyNot.3: Prepare premature closure is used when the board ends a project early; this project has run its full course.

B.q: Leah Whitfield prepares the end project report and lessons report for the Tarnside project. Dr Elaine Fairbairn, the executive, asks which role answers for the outcome of the 'evaluate the project' activity. Which role should be accountable?
B.why: The executive is accountable for evaluate the project; the PM is responsible for carrying it out (19.6, table 19.2).

whyNot.0: Leah is responsible for the activity, but accountability sits with the executive.
whyNot.1: The business layer is not involved in evaluate the project.
whyNot.3: Project assurance is consulted in evaluate the project.

B.q: Near the end of the Tarnside project, Leah Whitfield closes the project log, makes sure all project records are secured and archived in the college's records system, and prepares the closure communications. Which 'closing a project' activity is she carrying out?
B.why: Prepare planned closure includes closing the project log, securing and archiving project information and preparing closure communications (19.4.1).

whyNot.1: Evaluate the project REVIEWS the project log for lessons; closing it and archiving records is prepare planned closure.
whyNot.2: Confirm project acceptance is about handing products to operations and confirming acceptance.
whyNot.3: Request project closure is the briefing to the board that follows.

B.q: Leah Whitfield briefs the Tarnside project board on the project's performance and confirms the project is ready to close. She recommends that Greystack be considered for future college works and suggests the board thanks everyone involved. Which 'closing a project' activity is she carrying out?
B.why: In request project closure the PM briefs the board on performance, confirms readiness, highlights concessions and recommends celebrating success, including recognizing a high-performing supplier (19.4.5).

whyNot.0: Evaluate the project assesses performance and lessons; the recommendation to the board is made when requesting closure.
whyNot.1: Confirm project acceptance hands products over to operations.
whyNot.2: Prepare planned closure confirms the project can close and archives records; it does not brief the board.

C.q: In the final stage at Tarnside College, Leah Whitfield reviews the issue register and spots a lesson: the curriculum team was involved too late in the bay layout design. She includes it in the lessons report, which she prepares in consultation with the project management team. Is this an appropriate application of the 'evaluate the project' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because preparing planned closure closes the project log
Yes, because it draws lessons from the project log with the PMT
No, because lessons belong in the end stage report for the stage
No, because lessons are reviewed by the business after closure
C.why: Evaluate the project includes reviewing the project log, which includes the issue register, to identify lessons for future projects and including them in the lessons report in consultation with the PMT (19.4.4).

whyNot.0: Closing the project log is part of prepare planned closure, but that does not explain why reviewing it for lessons is appropriate here.
whyNot.2: End stage reports are produced at stage boundaries; the final stage ends with the lessons report and end project report.
whyNot.3: The business may use the lessons later, but identifying them is a closing activity for the PM.

C.q: Suppose that halfway through the Tarnside structural works, the combined authority withdraws the grant. Leah Whitfield decides herself to close the project, tells Greystack to stop work and begins preparing premature closure. Is this an appropriate application of the 'prepare premature closure' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because the business case is no longer valid without the grant
Yes, because closing a project can be tailored for an early close
No, because premature closure is triggered by the project board
No, because an exception plan must be approved before closure
C.why: The project board triggers a premature close, for example when the business case is no longer valid; the PM then prepares it (19.3).

whyNot.0: The business case may well be invalid, but the decision to close early belongs to the board, not the PM.
whyNot.1: Closing a project is tailored for a premature close, but that does not give the PM the authority to trigger it.
whyNot.3: No exception plan is needed before a premature close; the board can decide to close directly.

C.q: Leah Whitfield proposes keeping the Tarnside project open for six months after the centre opens, so that she can measure apprentice numbers before requesting closure. Is this an appropriate approach to closing the project, and why?
options: Yes, because the senior user must show that benefits are on track
Yes, because the grant can be clawed back if apprenticeships lag
No, because the executive measures benefits in the final stage
No, because post-project benefits reviews are planned, not performed
C.why: It is not a project activity to carry out post-project benefits reviews, only to plan them; the business carries them out after closure (19.4.3, 19.5.2).

whyNot.0: The senior user does stay committed to benefits, but after closure, not by keeping the project open.
whyNot.1: The clawback risk makes benefits reviews important, but they still happen after closure under the benefits management approach.
whyNot.2: Benefits after opening are reviewed by the business after the project, not measured by the executive in the final stage.

reteach.title: Hand over, look back, sign off
reteach.question: Think of closing a project as three moves: hand the products over, look back on how it went, and ask for sign-off. Which activity is each move?

blocks.body: After preparing planned (or premature) closure, the PM hands over: confirm project acceptance. Then looks back: evaluate the project, producing the end project report and lessons report. Then asks for sign-off: request project closure, after which the board authorizes closure in directing a project.

blocks.text: Evaluate the project RACI: executive accountable, PM responsible, senior supplier and project assurance consulted; the business layer is not involved.

explain.body: Planned closure confirms the project can close, updates the project plan with actuals, closes the project log, archives records and prepares closure communications. Premature closure, triggered by the board, records the request, salvages anything useful, makes products safe and agrees what is complete and what is abandoned.

test.q: Suppose the Tarnside project board decides to close the project early after the grant is withdrawn. Which action should Leah Whitfield take in 'prepare premature closure'?
options: Salvage useful work and make unfinished products safe
Carry out the post-project benefits reviews early
Prepare an exception plan for the remaining work
Hand the unfinished centre to estates as complete
test.why: Prepare premature closure records the request, salvages anything useful, makes products safe and agrees what is complete or abandoned (19.4.2).

whyNot.1: Post-project benefits reviews are planned by the project and carried out by the business after closure.
whyNot.2: An exception plan replaces a stage or project plan to continue; the board has decided to close.
whyNot.3: An orderly close agrees honestly what is complete and what is abandoned.

explain.body: The project's products must pass to an operational and maintenance environment before closure, in one release or in phases, and acceptance is confirmed. A check that post-project benefits reviews are planned may be done by the senior user.

test.q: Paul Kettering, a governor, asks Leah Whitfield what must happen to the centre's products before the Tarnside project can close. Which answer is correct?
options: They stay with Greystack until benefits are realized
They pass to the operational and maintenance environment
They are re-tendered to a new maintenance contractor
They are kept by the project for six months of checks
test.why: In confirm project acceptance, the products must be passed to an operational and maintenance environment before the project closes (19.4.3).

whyNot.0: Benefits are realized after closure by the business; the supplier does not keep the products until then.
whyNot.2: Handover goes to the people who will operate and maintain the products, here the estates team; re-tendering is not part of acceptance.
whyNot.3: The project should not drift on after delivery; a clear end transfers ownership to the business.

explain.body: The PM reviews the project's original intent in the baselined PID and the approved changes in its current version, compares estimates with actuals, reviews the project log for lessons with the PMT, and produces the lessons report and the end project report.

head: Product
Purpose
rows: Performance against the PID; product review; follow-on actions
Lessons for this and future projects

test.q: Leah Whitfield needs a report showing how the Tarnside project performed against the version of the PID used to authorize it, including a review of the products and recommendations for follow-on actions. Which product should she produce?
test.why: The end project report reviews performance against the PID used to authorize the project, with a product review and follow-on action recommendations; it is produced in evaluate the project.

whyNot.0: The lessons report passes on lessons; it does not review performance against the PID.
whyNot.1: End stage reports are produced at stage boundaries, which are not used at the end of the final stage.
whyNot.3: Highlight reports are routine stage reports from controlling a stage, not the closing review.

explain.body: Request project closure briefs the board on performance, confirms readiness, highlights concessions and recommends recognition. For evaluate the project, the executive is accountable, the PM responsible, and the senior supplier and project assurance consulted; the business layer is not involved.

test.q: Tarnside College's audit committee asks how responsibilities were split when the project was evaluated at closure. Which statement about the RACI for 'evaluate the project' is correct?
test.why: For evaluate the project, the executive is accountable and the PM responsible; the senior supplier and project assurance are consulted (19.6, table 19.2).

whyNot.0: This reverses the roles: the executive is accountable and the PM responsible.
whyNot.1: The business layer is not involved in evaluate the project.
whyNot.2: The executive is accountable, not responsible, and project assurance is consulted.
